original.target_description: Unassigned original side; not examined under replication-only blind validation.

replication.target_description: Study 1b: community pedestrian field sample; elderly versus neutral scrambled-sentence prime; walking time over an 81.7 m public walkway with no intervening task; prime main effect in ANOVA including median-split private self-consciousness. The supplied neutral description is broad; the study identifier and p. 4 locator identify this walking test.

n.sample_role: Community pedestrian participants; 40 approached/recruited is printed, but final analytic sample after the walking-route exclusions is not separately stated.
n.exclusions: Only pedestrians appearing under 50 were approached. Participants who stopped or did not proceed directly down the walkway were excluded; exclusion count not stated.

n.quote: Forty pedestrians were stopped on a central, grassy area in the local community and asked to participate in a class project. | Participants who did not proceed directly down the walkway without stopping were excluded from the study.

notes: Published article title, authors and DOI match the supplied replication reference. Extracted the elderly-versus-neutral prime main effect corresponding to the original walking-speed effect, rather than the self-consciousness interaction. No unambiguous standalone author replication-success category is assigned to this individual study; the authors explicitly claim replication only for combined Studies 1a/1b analyses, so reported_success remains null rather than inferring a verdict from p. The separately printed interaction is F(1, 36) = 6.77, p = .01. The reported residual df of 36 is retained but was not used to manufacture a separately printed final n. Combined analyses have residual df 60 and report prime-group Ns of 36 and 32, so these pooled sample counts cannot resolve the separate-study final n. Original side is an unassigned placeholder and was not consulted. Source version: published article supplied by licensed EBSCO PsycInfo service.
